note: Spans our own items share with the third-party books that a human reviewed and judged to be standard exam formulation rather than anyone's authorship. Each entry names the reason. This is a list of specific spans, not a loosened threshold - an over-permissive rule fails open and silently, a reviewed list does not.

spans.text: equation is true for all values of x where a b and c are constants
spans.why: The canonical College Board stem for coefficient matching. The clause 'is true for all values of x' is what distinguishes an identity from an equation to solve, and 'where a, b, and c are constants' is what tells the student which letters are unknowns. Both are doing work no paraphrase does as well, and the books carry them for the same reason we do: they are the exam's own wording, not the author's.

spans.text: equation is true for all values of x where a h and k are constants what is the value of
spans.why: The same stem with the vertex-form letters, followed by the standard closing question. Same reasoning.

spans.text: a circle in the xy plane what is the length of the
spans.why: Standard circle stem. 'a circle in the' appears in 31 College Board items and 'what is the length of the' in 6.

spans.text: is negative the parabola opens downward and the vertex is a maximum
spans.why: A statement of mathematical fact, in the only form it takes. 'the parabola opens downward' appears in 7 College Board items.

spans.text: are constants if the equation is true for all values of x what is the value of
spans.why: The coefficient-matching stem again, in its 'if ... what is the value of' order rather than the 'where ... are constants' order already listed. 'is true for all values of' appears in the College Board corpus.

spans.text: are constants if the equation has no solution which of the following could be the
spans.why: Standard no-solution stem. 'the equation has no solution' appears in 3 College Board items.

spans.text: are constants for which of the following values of
spans.why: Standard 'find the constant' stem. 'for which of the following values of' appears in 2 College Board items.

how_verified: Each span was searched for in College Board's own corpus with LaTeX stripped. All of them appear there, which settles the question: they are the exam's wording, carried by the books because the books teach the same exam. They did not clear the automatic College Board exemption only because an 8-word window straddles a variable position, where the two normalisers disagree - the corpus has LaTeX, the PDFs have loose glyphs.
